jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Solomon Islands has no AI law, national AI strategy or data protection law. Its only official AI-governance commitment is the 'AI for Government' initiative in the government ICT Services Digital Strategy 2026-2030, which plans a national AI governance framework and ethical AI guidelines for government. The education ministry has announced an AI-in-education policy but has not yet published it.
lead_institutions: SIG ICT Services (Ministry of Finance and Treasury)
Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from Parliament's, the government portal's and the ICT ministry's websites. No searchable online gazette was found. The education ministry's AI policy and ICT master plan, and the national cybersecurity policy, are not published online and are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: SIG ICT Services Digital - Data, People, Technology and Cyber Strategy 2026 - 2030
instruments.english_title: Solomon Islands Government ICT Services Digital - Data, People, Technology and Cyber Strategy 2026-2030
instruments.issuing_authority: Solomon Islands Government ICT Services (Ministry of Finance and Treasury)
instruments.current_status: Published September 2025 by SIG ICT Services and described in the forewords as fully endorsed by the government; it covers 2026-2030, with Initiative 28 (AI for Government) and the AI element of Initiative 9 scheduled January 2026 - December 2030. No resulting AI governance framework or SIG AI-use guidelines had been published on official sites as of 2026-10-13.
instruments.summary: Whole-of-government digital strategy of the Solomon Islands Government ICT Services (foreword by the Minister for Finance and Treasury) for 2026-2030, organised around data, people, technology and cyber pillars and 28 initiatives. Initiative 28 'AI for Government: Governance, Capability & Public Value' targets ethical, transparent use of AI across government through a cross-agency working group, a co-designed AI Governance Framework, AI literacy capability assessments, training and pilot AI applications, with a national AI governance framework as a deliverable. Initiative 9 (Data Governance Policies) adds 'AI Policy Integration': guidelines for the ethical use of AI within SIG covering data governance, privacy and security compliance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Only official Solomon Islands document found that sets government objectives for AI governance; it commits to a national AI governance framework and SIG guidelines on ethical AI use.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Solomon Islands' parliament bill lists, the communications ministry, government ICT services, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for binding law, ethics, risk and assurance, procurement, cybersecurity, data and privacy, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sectoral rules, generative AI, drafts, international agreements or historical publications. The regional legal information search was unavailable, no searchable online gazette was found, and the full texts of the ICT for Education Master Plan 2026-2030 and the National Cybersecurity Policy 2024 are not online, so these remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. PacLII search 403; no searchable online gazette; parliament Acts list not text-searched act by act. Bills 2023-2026 listed; Public Service Bill 2025, Education Bill 2023 searched: no AI. National ICT Policy 2017, ICT Strategic Plan 2019-2023, ICT Services Technical Standard 2025: no AI. Digital Strategy dated 2025-09 ('Published September 2025'). CBSI sandbox mentions only algorithms (lead). Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: parliament.gov.sb bills 2023-2026 listed (no AI, data-protection, cybercrime or online-safety bill; Public Service Bill 2025 and Education Bill 2023 text-searched, no AI/automated-decision provisions); MCA relevant-legislation list (Telecommunications Act 2009 etc., no AI). No data protection or cybercrime statute exists. Searched, nothing found. PacLII search blocked (403).; Government: SIG ICT Services Digital Strategy 2026-2030 recorded (AI for Government initiative). MCA National ICT Policy 2017 and National Broadcast Policy: no AI content. SIG Five-Year ICT Strategic Plan 2019-2023 and SIG ICTS Technical Standard 2025: no AI content. No national AI strategy or public-sector AI guideline found.; Ministries: Education (MEHRD): AI education policy announced (lead), ICT for Education Master Plan 2026-2030 launched but text not online (lead). Health: digital health strategy 2025-2029, no official text/AI content found. Justice, police, finance (other than ICT Services), labour, home affairs: solomons.gov.sb search shows only AI awareness/training news, no AI documents. Searched, nothing found.; Regulators: No data protection authority or national cyber security agency issuing guidance (SICERT is a project). CBSI: regulatory sandbox framework read, no AI provisions (lead); no AI guidance. TCSI: no AI documents. Searched, nothing found.. Not reached: PacLII full-text search of Solomon Islands legislation (HTTP 403); parliament.gov.sb Acts list not individually text-searched; Solomon Islands Gazette (no searchable online gazette found). Could not verify: ICT for Education Master Plan 2026-2030 full text (not online); National Cybersecurity Policy 2024 full text (not online); PacLII legislation search (403). binding-law, ethics, risk-assurance, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development (MEHRD)
leads.note: Launched by the Minister of Education, Hon. Tozen Leokana, per the government notice https://solomons.gov.sb/mehrd-launches-solomon-islands-ict-for-education-master-plan-2026-2030/ (dated 16/04/2026), which says the Plan 'recognises the opportunities presented by Artificial Intelligence, while also calling for strong safeguards around ethics, child protection, equity, cyber safety'. Full text not found on mehrd.gov.sb (home page still links only the 2019-2023 ICT in Education Master Plan, which has no AI content) or solomons.gov.sb on 2026-10-13. Read when published and record (sectoral/education) if it sets AI expectations; otherwise keep as lead.

leads.note: Announcement of intent only: government notice https://solomons.gov.sb/govt-committed-to-developing-an-education-policy-on-artificial-intelligence-learning/ (18/02/2025) reports the Minister's 13 February 2025 statement that the government will develop an AI-driven education policy (National AI in-Education Strategy, AI literacy, ethical AI and data privacy regulation). Later reports describe a policy on student AI use in examinations as still being developed. No official document found as of 2026-10-13.

leads.note: Official PDF https://www.cbsi.com.sb/sites/default/files/2026-06/CBSI_RSB_Framework_final.pdf (linked from https://www.cbsi.com.sb/financial-stability/regulations/regulatory-sandbox); generic fintech sandbox launched 14 April 2022 per CBSI notice. Text does not mention AI; only an annex objective on assessing MSME creditworthiness 'using alternative data, data analytics and algorithms'. Out of scope unless CBSI states the sandbox covers AI (CBSI articles mention AI-based credit scoring products tested in it).
